Great location, unfortunately service is very poor.
Jul 2015 • Solo
Elle Café is located on the ground floor of the Bitexco tower. The outside seating area is really impressive and comfortable, an ideal place for a coffee of something to eat. The coffee is fantastic and the food is good too. Unfortunately, it has really poor waitress service. I have visited many times and it is difficult to get someone to take your order and even more difficult to get someone`s attention to pay the bill. The staff would much sooner huddle around the outside bar area playing with their phones or just chatting to each other. No wonder the café is usually empty even when all places nearby are busy! Its a real shame as the coffee and location are really good, hence why I continue to go despite the poor service. I hope someday a new manager will take over and make improvements to bring it up to standard, as it deserves to succeed on location alone.

A rip-off!!!
Sep 2014 • Solo
I have spent the past few weeks travelling through Vietnam and have a good idea of what to expect. I decided to sit down at Elle Cafe as it had great street appeal and was near my hotel. I just ordered a Vietnamese Coffee - White. Throughout my travels, I have been charged between 15,000 - 50,000dong for the coffee, so when I noticed in the menu that it was 65,000dong, I found it a but excessive, but decided that it was a nice venue and I was happy to pay the price.

When I went to pay, I noticed the bill quoted 71,500dong as VAT had been added to the cost.

Throughout my entire trip, I have not once had VAT added to the price - in fact, it is not customary of Vietnam to do so!! The addition of VAT to the price is nothing but a ploy to fool others and gain more money. 

I won't be supporting this cafe and its incorrect practises.

Much better choices nearby, keep walking
Jan 2014 • Friends
The setting for Elle Cafe and the ambiance in the evening is very inviting. Clearly they are catering to a western/tourist clientele. 

Unfortunately the food and the service do not live up to a venue pricing itself at a premium. We ordered garlic bread which turned out to be pathetic wafer thin little toasts - a rip-off at 100,000 Vietnamese Dong or 5US Dollars!

The menu is quite short - mains including only 3 pizza choices and 5 pasta choices. The pork medallion with peppercorn sauce is not served with vegetables and it took much effort to request this from the waitress.

Our main meals arrived in such irregular order that the first three had finished their meals before the last one had received theirs. 

The pasta servings were small and unfortunately the arrabiata was way too spicey for western palates leaving lips and tongues numb. 

Our first order of beers was cold but the second round was warm and we were unable to drink them.

All round this was a very disappointing evening and was very expensive by Ho Chi Minh standards.

The setting of Cafe Elle has such potential but appears to have been let down by poor management.
